title: 5 resume mistakes killing your resume and how to fix them fast!
description:

In this video, I share all of the fixes that will get your resume noticed and score interviews. Stick around if you want recruiters contacting you in no time!

It's because your resume isn't quickly showing your value, and you may be falling into common mistakes that are killing your chances. There are five common mistakes that instantly send résumés to the digital [music] trash pile. But don't panic. I've got your back. I'm a career strategist with over 20 years of experience helping hundreds of job seekers land great opportunities. The biggest mistake and the one I see most often is that your resume reads like a job description. This is a huge deal breaker. Employers don't want a simple list of what you did. They want to see the value you bring, the impact you can make, and how you can solve problems. Here's an example of a weak bullet point that sounds more like a job description for a role in fundraising and development. wrote and secured major grants from foundations. This is just restating a duty that almost any fundraising candidate would have. It tells the employer nothing about you, your skills, or your impact. There's no context, no metrics, no story. Here's a much stronger version. achieved a 90% grant award rate through strategic research and persuasive proposal writing, securing major funding from the United Way and VA to launch two new programs, doubling service capacity. This communicates multiple things. You're skilled in strategic research, clear and compelling proposal writing, and it shows your impact. You have a 90% grant award rate, major new funding, and doubling service capacity. It also demonstrates versatility. You have been successful with both private grants and government grants. The additional experience section can also highlight work older than 10 years. Show relevant technical skills or include transferable experiences if you're pivoting into new roles. Keep the main resume focused concise and impactful while still demonstrating your full expertise. Finally, don't overdesign your resume.
